title: Tail-latency-aware autoscale validation & customer acceptance bench harness
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Build a reproducible benchmarking and acceptance harness that validates autoscaling policies and fleet controls against tail-latency SLOs for Dedicated customers. This ticket covers design and implementation of a harness that synthesizes realistic request mixes, replays sampled customer traffic, and injects burst/failure modes to ensure autoscalers (elastic-slice and burst-coordinator) meet configurable percentile targets (95th/99th token/service latency) under both steady-state and ramp scenarios. The harness must be portable to customer onboarding runs and produce an acceptance report consumable by Sales/CS. Deliverables: reusable load agent, workload templates (conversational/embedding/rerank), instrumentation hooks for Console dashboards, acceptance-run checklist, and a regression test suite for CI to prevent regressions in autoscale behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a 30-minute sustained mixed workload (token gen + embeddings) with configurable QPS and concurrency
Autoscaling policies validated against target SLOs: 95th <= 150ms and 99th <= 450ms for guided small-model profile; thresholds configurable per customer
Support injection of node failures and region fallbacks; acceptance run includes graceful fallback verification
Generated acceptance report includes charts for p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, autoscaler decisions (scale-up/down events), kernel utilization, and per-model token cost
Playbook for customer-run acceptance (steps, expected outputs, pass/fail criteria) documented and linked
CI regression job runs a fast smoke variant and fails on SLO regressions with diffable artifacts
test_plan: Phase 1 - Minimal harness: implement generator with template-driven prompts and token distributions (estimated 2d)
Phase 2 - Autoscaler hooks: emit scale decision events and validate policy parameters (3d)
Phase 3 - Failure injection: simulate GPU eviction, network partition, and delayed KV cache (2d)
Phase 4 - Customer replay: add sampled-replay mode to play a sanitized customer trace; provide CLI option to map endpoints to customer models (3d)
Phase 5 - Acceptance report + playbook: assemble artifacts, example run, and customer-facing checklist (2d)
Phase 6 - CI integration: add smoke job to pipeline and baseline comparison tooling (1d)
observability_instructions: Instrument with Console trace tags: bench.run_id, bench.template, customer_id (optional), autoscaler_policy
Export per-request telemetry to bench-specific dashboard: token_latencies_ms, request_count, model_kv_hit_ratio, gpu_util_pct
Attach GPU and host metrics: GPU memory pressure, kernel latency breakdown, network egress (MB/s)
Persist raw request logs (sampled) and the autoscaler event timeline for offline analysis
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Synthetic workloads may miss real-world burst patterns. Mitigation: support sampled customer replay and ensure templates include uncommon long-context tails
Risk: Acceptance runs may be noisy on shared infra. Mitigation: pin test runs to dedicated sandbox pool or use isolated tenant on Dedicated
Risk: CI regression false positives. Mitigation: maintain a short smoke variant with looser thresholds and require manual triage for full-run failures
Risk: Large artifact storage from raw traces. Mitigation: default retention 7 days and gated export for customers
implementation_notes: Use existing prober infra from ENG-11522 as a reference for transport and throttling primitives
Load agent will be built in Go to reuse our k8s client and low-latency HTTP libs; provide a thin Python wrapper for engineers who need ad-hoc runs
Workload templates stored in a YAML library with variable placeholders for model, sequence_length, and prompt complexity
Autoscaler validation module will subscribe to scale events emitted by runtime and correlate with latency spikes to compute decision lag
